newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Prime Minister Bhutto subpoenaed in funds probe.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Prime Minister Bhutto subpoenaed in funds probe.

text.p: A U.S. Justice Department task force probing fund-raising abuses during the 1996 election is seeking to question former Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto about efforts by Representative Dan Burton to pressure a lobbyist for her government to raise campaign contributions for him, the Washington Post reported Saturday.

Quoting unidentified government officials, the newspaper said Bhutto, who is on a lecture tour in Indiana and Washington state, was served with a subpoena earlier this week requiring her to appear before a federal grand jury hearing evidence in the investigation.

The grand jury, which is conducting a broad review of fund-raising practices in the congressional and presidential elections, already has questioned Mark Siegel, the lobbyist for the former Bhutto government about whether he was "shaken down" for contributions by Burton.
Burton, an Indiana Republican, is heading a House investigation of Democratic fund-raising practices.

Siegel made the claim in a July 25 memo to the Bhutto government, saying Burton threatened that "none of his friends or colleagues" would meet with the lobbyist or his associates because of Siegel's failure to raise $5,000 in campaign contributions from Pakistani-Americans.
